column2: Scots, Irish, Welsh, and Cornish alike once bent the knee to a single British crown. Reactionary voices in Parliament argue that a divided Albion is an insult to history, and that the whole of the isles are England's by ancient right.

Long before the Union, Scottish kings held Cumbria and planted their own settlers deep into Ulster's soil. The border counties and the Ulster plantations both once answered to Edinburgh, and reactionary lairds insist they should again.

Centuries before Scotland had a name, Irish kings ruled both sides of the North Channel as one kingdom. Argyll and the Hebrides were settled from Ulster first, and reactionary voices in Dublin call it long past time to reclaim them.
